storm.summary_layperson: No storms on radar right now and no watches or warnings are up — there's a slight chance of a shower or thunderstorm building in later this evening, but nothing organized is currently tracking toward the cove.
storm.local_effect_blurb: Air-water gap is a healthy 8.5°F at 4 PM but fades to about 3°F by 8 PM as the air cools, and there's no storm in the pipeline right now for that buffer to act on either way.
storm.detail_html:
Radar (KOKX) is clear — no cells anywhere near the cove, and no NWS watches, warnings, or advisories are active. CAPE is a modest 720 J/kg with strong 0-6km bulk shear aloft (49 kt from the west), but that shear isn't currently organizing anything since there's no convection to work with. The OKX area forecast discussion (issued 2:21 PM) mentions a "late afternoon to evening window for a good coverage of showers and thunderstorms passing from west to east," with severe chances called "less certain" — that's a general regional mention, not a tracked cell. A separate AFD note about a frontal system bringing heavier rain applies to Sunday, three days out, not tonight.

The Sound's usual protective marine layer is a moving target through the window. Water is 73.9°F against 82.4°F air right now — an 8.5°F gap — but that's a snapshot, not a fixed condition: air cools after sunset while the Sound stays flat, so the gap is projected to fall under the ~5°F protective threshold around 7:30 PM, down to roughly 3°F by 8 PM and essentially gone by 9 PM. Right now the mechanism isn't even flagged as active (marine layer strength reads "moderate," not strong enough on its own).

Net effect: if a cell does organize to the west earlier in the evening, it would arrive into at least a partial buffer; anything developing after about 7:30 PM would find little to none. With nothing on radar and CAPE well under the 1,500 J/kg threshold that would flag moderate risk on its own, there's nothing here to call amplifying or mitigating — it's a non-event right now either way.

Bottom line: nothing to act on. Worth a radar recheck closer to sunset given the AFD's mention of a west-to-east shower/thunderstorm window this evening, but as of this run the cove is clear.

wind.regime_label: Light gradient wind — sea breeze not filling in

hourly.shift_note: light, backing to W after sunset

wind.tactics_blurb: Despite a solid 8.5°F air-water gap, the sea breeze never fills onto the coast tonight (just 21% of coastal stations reading southerly) — expect straight light W/WNW gradient flow around 6 kt easing to 3-4 kt after sunset. Favor the center of the course and treat any shifts as small and persistent rather than tactical oscillations.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
This reads as a gradient-wind evening, not a sea-breeze day, even though the air-water temperature difference (deltaT) is a strong 8.5°F — normally plenty to seed a thermal. The two-ingredient sea-breeze test needs deltaT above 5°F and the breeze actually filling in at the coast; only 21% of coastal stations are reading southerly, well short of a filled thermal, and the pipeline's own sea-breeze-active check reads false. The one place the thermal is showing up is over open water — buoy 44040 is fully southerly — but it isn't making it onto the CT shore.

What you'll actually feel is a light W-to-WNW synoptic flow, about 7.7 kt on the wider gradient measure, easing through the window (6 kt at the start, down to 3-4 kt by 8-9 PM). That's offshore-over-land character: channeled down the Sound from the NYC direction, steady in bearing but with holes near the CT shore and better average pressure mid-Sound. As it backs toward NW late in the window it gets a bit puffier. Favor the center of the cove away from the immediate shore lee rather than committing to either side.

Shift character is persistent, not oscillating — this is straight synoptic flow, not a mature thermal, so there's no clean cyclical shift to play. HRRR has the direction wandering slowly across the window (WNW around 285-292° early, backing to W near 272° around sunset, then swinging to NW 303-310° after dark) rather than the tight oscillations a mature sea breeze would give — treat any single swing as a small header or lift, not a play-both-ways shift.

Worth flagging: the wider ensemble currently reads WSW (258-265°) while HRRR's forecast opens at W (274-284°), an 11-16° gap — modest, and since this isn't a Regime A/A+ day the sea-breeze maturation correction doesn't apply anyway. RYC itself (ground truth for the cove) is light and W right now: 263° at 1.7 kt, gusting 7.6, 10-min average 3.9 kt.

Bottom line for the fleet: a light, patient evening in the 3-6 kt range with gusts to 9-10 kt early, drifting into drifter territory (3-4 kt) after 8 PM. Not a postponement-risk breeze, but not powered-up racing either. Sunset (7:55 PM) doesn't change much here since there's no thermal to collapse — if anything, expect direction to get a touch more erratic backing NW after dark as the boundary layer stabilizes.

data_caveats: Buoy 44040 wind/air observation is about 76 min old and the WLIS SST reading is about 88 min old — treat offshore sea-breeze depth and marine-layer numbers as based on slightly stale data.
22:00 hour of the wind table draws from HRRR's extended outlook (f07+), lower confidence than the primary f01-f06 window.
